method: I started from all 658 companies the notes cover. A quick screen on each note's growth estimate and today's P/E kept about 70 that might earn 20% a year or more; reading their notes removed those with governance problems (heavy promoter pledges, qualified audits, money moving to promoters) or profit that does not turn into cash. That left 40, mostly fast growers. Because those mostly failed on price, I added 12 cheaper, steadier companies (Sharda Cropchem, SBI, Gulf Oil and others) so the list was not tilted to one style: 52 in all.

Each of the 52 got a deep dive: both of its latest calls read in full, its filed figures from Screener, everything its note says, and anything announced since. For each I set a clean profit base (one-offs removed), built profit year by year to FY30 from orders, capacity, margins, interest and tax, and haircut the promises of managements that have missed before.

The selling price is the heart of it, as you said: what P/E the market pays in March 2030 depends on how much growth is still ahead then. I used one scale for every company: about 10–15 times profit for growth under 8% a year, 14–20 for 8–12%, 18–26 for 12–16%, 24–34 for 16–20%, 30–42 for 20–25% and at most 50 above that, lower in each band for weak cash, debt, governance or one big customer, and checked against peers and each stock's own history.

Return a year = (FY30 profit × that P/E, less any new shares the company issues) against today's market value, over the time left to March 2030, plus dividends. The bad case lowers profit for the most likely disappointment and takes the P/E down one band. Each card also shows what you would earn if the market kept paying today's P/E, because that one assumption decides most of the answer.

The honest result: at today's prices only V2 Retail clears 25% in the normal case, and it is a starter because it has not yet produced cash. Five more come within three points (J Kumar, CleanMax, Samhi, Sunteck, M&B). Most of the popular growth names (defence, electronics, power equipment, platforms) return under 10% a year on these rules, because they already trade at 60–150 times profit. The last six of the twelve are good businesses at 17–19% today; each card shows the market value at which it would clear 25%.

Conviction: High would mean clearing 25% with room and a bad case that still makes money (none today). Medium is within reach of 25%, or clears it with one weak spot. Starter clears it but carries a real flag. On a dip means worth owning, but only below the value shown. Your limits are built into the weights column: at most 20% in one stock and 40% in one theme.

Another related-party disposal or a goodwill write-down.

Visa applications flat at 11.3 lakh in Q1 FY27; revenue per application now 'stabilised'.

Goodwill ₹1,213cr, about half of equity; value created by deals not quantified.

profitBase.label: year to June 2026
profitBase.note: EPL alone: ₹393cr plus ~₹10–15cr Q4 FY26 merger costs, tax normalised to 21%; Indovida adds ₹410cr (2025), pro-forma ₹810cr on 50.5cr shares

base.exitPeWhy: Lower half of 14–20 for 10–12% growth: tube moat and low debt, but a third-plus of profit from preforms under a resin-seller controller; below EPL's 18.5 today.

bad.what: Indovida stays near its weak 2025 profit, Europe doesn't recover (margin 18.5%) and no synergies arrive.

ideas.tailRisk: Indorama, the PET resin maker that will control and supply the merged company, could set related-party terms against minority holders; the merger could also slip or fail.

scoreWhy.balanceSheet: Net debt ₹581cr (0.58x operating profit), falling to about 0.25x with Indovida's net cash; AA+ ratings on merger watch.
scoreWhy.earningsQuality: 82% of FY22–FY26 operating profit became cash, but stock days rose every year to 177 and tax swings 14–22%.
scoreWhy.management: Beat the revenue guide and recovered all Q1 cost inflation, but profit fell 1.4%, Europe is at 4.8% EBIT, the MD is new and control passes to the supplier.
scoreWhy.moatRunway: World number one in laminated tubes (about 20% share, a third of oral care), qualified on customer lines; beauty runway long; preforms less differentiated.

ideas.oneLine: A world-leading tube maker whose merger lifts profit per share about 28%, but 13% growth at 16x gives about 19% a year.
whyOwn: Indovida earned ₹410cr in 2025, about as much as EPL, for 58% more shares, so profit per share rises about 28% on completion with no cash paid.
Q1 FY27 revenue rose 25% (20% underlying) and all polymer, freight and currency inflation was recovered; guidance was raised to high-teens growth.
Beauty and personal care is now 54% of tubes and growing 20%+, with an aim to double beauty share from 8% to 16%.
mustGoRight: The merger completes by about Q4 FY27 on the agreed swap, with dividends resuming.
Indovida's profit grows at least 8% a year from ₹410cr and EPL holds a 20% margin.
Related-party resin purchases from Indorama disclosed and priced at arm's length.
breaksIt: The merger delayed past FY27 or its terms changed against EPL holders.
EPL's underlying margin below 18% for two quarters, or Europe still below 8% EBIT by Q4 FY27.
Large related-party purchases from Indorama without independent pricing disclosure.
worstFacts: Merger adds about 58% more shares and gives 51.8% control to Indorama, a resin maker and supplier.
Indovida's 2025 sales and volumes fell; its Q2 2026 profit jump looks crisis-driven.
Q1 FY27 profit fell 1.4% on a 22% tax rate.
Stock days up every year since FY21 to 177.
Europe earned only 4.8% at the EBIT level in Q1 FY27.
No dividend until the merger completes.
New MD since January 2026, new to packaging.
nextChecks: Q2 FY27 revenue growth of 17%+ with an underlying margin near 20%.
Europe EBIT margin moving up from 4.8% towards 10%+.
Tribunal and shareholder meeting dates for the merger; Indovida's Q3 2026 profit versus THB 1.3bn in Q2.

profitBase.note: Added back about ₹8cr after-tax exceptional item in Q3 FY26; Q1 FY27 bad-debt provision left in.

base.exitPeWhy: Lower half of the 14–20 band: capital-hungry, negative free cash and cyclical; matches its 13.5–18 P/E history and today's 14.7.

bad.what: Wind additions stall, Saudi cranes arrive late or idle and Gulf collections stay slow while debt costs still arrive.

ideas.tailRisk: Old sales-tax demands on crane hire of ₹70–160cr each, not counted as contingent liabilities, against ₹1,311cr of net worth.

scoreWhy.balanceSheet: Net debt ₹545cr is 1.3 times operating profit, but rising toward a ₹1,000–1,100cr ceiling with ₹652cr of FY27 capex.
scoreWhy.earningsQuality: Operating cash covers 65–100% of operating profit, but free cash was negative two years and Gulf clients take 201 days.
scoreWhy.management: On track for FY27 guidance with better disclosure, but the Saudi pipeline was cut within a quarter and the MD's pay needed ratification.
scoreWhy.moatRunway: World's third-largest crane fleet with few rivals for the biggest cranes, but growth needs ever more capex and follows project cycles.

ideas.oneLine: A strong crane franchise growing 25–30%, but debt-funded cranes eat the gain; about 19% a year at ₹350.
whyOwn: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 39% to ₹380cr with cranes 86% used; order book ₹1,253cr covers FY27.
FY27 EBITDA guided at ₹525–575cr against ₹429cr, and FY28 at ₹650–700cr; Q1 is on track.
Gulf cranes earn a 4.1% monthly yield against 2.29% in India; ₹324cr of new Gulf cranes arrive in H2 FY27.
mustGoRight: ₹560cr of H2 FY27 cranes, including the Saudi fleet, arrive on time and run above 80% use.
Gulf debtor days fall from 201 toward 150 and the bad-debt provision reverses.
India's wind additions rise toward 7.5 GW in FY27 and keep the wind E&C business growing at 12–15% margins.
breaksIt: FY27 EBITDA below ₹500cr (guide ₹525–575cr).
Net debt above ₹1,100cr before FY28 EBITDA reaches ₹650cr.
Gulf debtor days above 200 again in the September quarter.
worstFacts: Margin fell from 63% in FY24 to 33% in Q1 FY27 as low-margin wind construction grew.
Free cash flow negative: −₹75cr in FY25 and −₹130cr in FY26.
Gulf customers take 201 days to pay; ₹6.2cr bad-debt provision in Q1.
Saudi pipeline cut from $50m to $38m in one quarter; Saudi arm lost about ₹10cr in FY26.
Old sales-tax demands of ₹70–160cr each not shown as contingent liabilities.
MD's ₹6.46cr pay exceeded the listing-rule limit; independent director resigned in September.
nextChecks: H1 FY27 EBITDA at least ₹245cr, on track for ₹525cr+ (Q1: ₹139cr company basis).
Gulf debtor days below 170 and group below 110 in the September quarter.
Net debt at September below ₹800cr while H2 cranes are ordered.

base.exitPeWhy: About 14% growth after FY30; middle of the 18–26 band: 26% returns and low debt against 48% cash conversion and small size; matches its own five-year median of 23.

bad.what: The new plant ramps slowly, volume grows about 8%, aluminium falls back and the margin slips to 10%.

ideas.tailRisk: A large private customer such as Adani or Birla moving its cable buying to its own new cable business.

scoreWhy.balanceSheet: Net debt about ₹15cr at March 2026 and only about 24% of bank limits used, but ₹208cr of guarantees and promoters' personal guarantees.
scoreWhy.earningsQuality: 48% of five years' operating profit (₹210cr of ₹435cr) became cash; FY26 free cash only about ₹5cr.
scoreWhy.management: Margin promise kept for nine quarters, but the new plant is 15–18 months late and its rating was withdrawn at its own request.
scoreWhy.moatRunway: Utility, Power Grid and US approvals with 80–90% metal pass-through, but many rivals are adding capacity.

ideas.oneLine: Disciplined 26%-return cable maker at a fair 22 times profit; about 17% a year, so buy below about ₹380 or on proof of faster growth.
whyOwn: Operating margin held at 10.3–11.4% for nine quarters through a 59% aluminium rise, because 80–90% of orders pass metal through.
26% return on capital and net debt of only about ₹15cr; high-voltage cables rose to 68% of sales from 35% in FY19.

The ₹40–45cr Reengus plant can add about ₹240–250cr of sales (about a fifth more) once ramped up over three to four quarters (Q2 FY27 call); exports reached 13% of Q1 sales but fell to 8% in H1 as US shipments stalled.
mustGoRight: The Reengus plant starts in October–November 2026 and reaches 80% use by March 2028.
Volume growth returns to 12–15% once metal prices settle, with the order book rising above ₹1,000cr.
Operating margin stays at 10.5% or more.
breaksIt: The Reengus plant not producing by March 2027.
Operating margin below 9.5% for two quarters.
Order book still at or below ₹811cr in March 2027.
worstFacts: New plant 15–18 months late; no start announced by 16 October.
Volume grew only 5–6% in Q1 and about 6% in Q2; growth is price-led.
Order book only ₹829cr in September 2026, up from about ₹811cr for two quarters.
Only 48% of five years' operating profit became cash.
India Ratings withdrew its rating at the company's request.
MD's daughter (HR head) and GM Quality resigned in September 2026.
nextChecks: Q3 FY27: the Reengus plant producing, and volume growth above 6%.
Operating margin back to at least 10.5% (Q2 was 10%).
Order book above ₹850cr at December 2026.

base.exitPeWhy: Middle of 14–20 / bottom of 18–26 for about 12% growth; resin exposure, 50% cash conversion and half the group audited by others keep it near today's 18.

bad.what: Volume grows only 8–10% (CRISIL), composite cylinders stay on hold, margin slips to 13–14% and working capital stays above 110 days.

scoreWhy.earningsQuality: Only 50% of FY22–FY26 operating profit became cash (26% in FY26); free cash −₹137cr in FY26; working capital 127 days.
scoreWhy.management: Meets profit guides (FY26 +21%, Q1 +22%) but missed volume twice; MD doubles as CFO; deal-size discrepancy; ₹340cr of share-sale money idle.
scoreWhy.moatRunway: About 55% of India's industrial packaging and composite approvals, but packaging is a commodity and composites wait on the oil companies.

ideas.oneLine: A steady 15–16% compounder at a fair 18x, but weak cash conversion caps the exit multiple; about 17% a year.
whyOwn: Profit rose from ₹316cr (FY24) to ₹477cr (FY26), and FY27 guidance was raised to 23–24% profit growth after Q1 delivered +22%.

Volume growth of at least 11% a year, with composites growing 25%.
Idle share-sale money (about ₹340cr) used for a buyback or a sensible deal, not left in deposits.

Volume growth below 8% for two quarters.
Any auditor qualification on the overseas subsidiaries or a large unexplained acquisition.
worstFacts: Only 26% of FY26 operating profit became cash; five-year conversion 50%; FY26 free cash −₹137cr.
Nine subsidiaries with ₹3,092cr revenue audited by other firms; MD is also CFO.
Volume missed the 15% guide: 13.5% in FY26, 11% in Q1 FY27.
Oil companies paused the 14.2-kg composite LPG cylinder.
Systoverse deal: ₹25cr in slides vs ₹125–150cr by the MD; ₹340cr of share-sale money idle.
Promoter stake down to 47.5%; TPL Plastech merger adds 1.6% shares.

changes.text: Samhi Hotels: all four Q2 FY27 checks met — same-store revenue +12.6% with RevPAR about +14% (rates +9%), margin 36.1% reported (39.1% before the GST cost), net debt down to ₹1,458cr at 3.1x, and no shares sold. No trigger hit; numbers kept; checks rolled to Q3. Also: J Kumar Infra's Q2 revenue of ₹1,539cr was just under its ₹1,550cr check, but H1 (₹3,050cr) and the 14.9% margin met theirs; no trigger hit, nothing changed.

Sharda Cropchem: break trigger hit — volume fell a second straight quarter (−5.1% in Q2 FY27 after −1.6%), as Europe's drought kept distributors from restocking. Other checks were met: sales ₹1,052cr (+13% on price and mix), gross margin 35.9%, operating margin 15.6%, registrations 3,044; but FY27 registration spending rose to ₹550–600cr. Revenue and margin guides kept, so FY30 profit is unchanged, and at today's price it still earns about 22% a year. Kept in the twelve for now; the owner is asked to decide (Needs a session). If Q3 volume falls again, swap it for the best reserve name (Mahindra Lifespace, about 22% at today's price).

Clean Max: H1 FY27 filing showed EBITDA of ₹1,011cr (check met), profit up six-fold to ₹120cr and the ₹3,000cr+ FY28 EBITDA floor kept, but 550 MW commissioned against the 600 MW check, and ₹2,500cr raised in green bonds (debt, not shares). No trigger hit; numbers kept; checks rolled to Q3.

Sunteck Realty: of the three Q2 checks, one was met (Oshiwara commercial construction under way; borrowings ₹940cr, under ₹1,000cr), one partly (pre-sales ₹824cr, but H1 collections ₹780cr against ₹850cr) and one missed (no Nepean Sea Road RERA; now promised before March 2027). No trigger hit; Dubai was already in the bad case. Numbers kept; checks rolled to Q3.

Dynamic Cables: Q2 call missed all three next checks (plant not yet producing, volume +6%, order book ₹829cr, margin 10%) but hit no trigger; the plant’s sales potential is now put at ₹240–250cr, too small a change to move FY30 profit. Numbers kept; checks rolled to Q3.
